bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Bahubali Plans To Invite 400,000 Guests For Daughter's Wedding - Rediff.com NEWS X News Business Movies Sports Cricket Get Ahead Company Email Rediff.com » News Bihar Bahubali Plans To Invite 400,000 Guests For Daughter's Wedding November 09, 2026 Expelled Janata Dal-United MLA Anant Singh , a known Bahubali, plans to invite people he knows in India and Pakistan for his daughter's marriage in the last week of November. Anant Singh said his daughter's wedding will be a mega event with more than 150 varieties of delicacies cooked for 400,000 guests. He plans to invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , Lalu Prasad Yadav , Nitish Kumar and Bhojpuri film stars for the wedding. The Supreme Court has directed Anant Singh to surrender to the authorities on December 1 in connection with the murder of Dularchand Yadav. -- M I KHAN © 2026 Rediff.com Disclaimer | Privacy Policy | Grievances | About us | Terms of use

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar health department plans to recruit 11,000 staff, notification likely in November
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar health department plans to recruit 11,000 staff, notification likely in November Subscribe to Notifications Written By : Rumela De Sarkar Published On 2026-11-09 04:00 GMT | Update On 2026-11-09 04:00 GMT Patna: Over 11,000 staff members are likely to be recruited for government healthcare facilities across Bihar , with the State Health Society , Bihar (SHSB) expected to release the official recruitment notification in the last week of November. According to an official release, the proposed recruitment drive will cover medical support, technical, administrative and clerical positions, aiming to address manpower shortages across the state's public healthcare system. Also Read:Karnataka to appoint 185 specialist doctors at District and Taluk Hospitals SHSB executive director Naval Kishor Choudhary said on Wednesday that preparations for the recruitment process were in the final stages. According to an official release, the detailed recruitment calendar will be issued after the department receives the necessary approvals, reports Urban Acres. As part of the preparations, the State Health Society is collecting updated vacancy details from all 38 districts of Bihar. The exercise covers district hospitals, sub-divisional hospitals, primary health centres (PHCs) and community health centres (CHCs). The updated data will help the department identify vacant positions and determine the final distribution of posts. The first phase of recruitment will cover several important categories, including staff nurses, laboratory technicians, block health managers, managerial personnel, non-medical establishment staff and clerical employees. Recruitment for other categories will be undertaken in the second phase, Choudhary said. The proposed appointments are intended to address manpower shortages from the district level to the panchayat level. Additional staff are expected to support doctors and paramedical personnel, particularly at healthcare facilities serving rural and remote areas. The recruitment drive is expected to improve the functioning of several sections of Bihar's public health system. Additional nurses and laboratory technicians will help strengthen patient care and diagnostic services, while block health managers and clerical employees will support the implementation and monitoring of government health schemes. The department also expects the appointments to reduce the workload on existing personnel at district and sub-divisional hospitals, improving the overall delivery of healthcare services. The hiring process will include selection, document verification and the issuance of appointment letters. Choudhary said the department aims to complete the entire process within six to seven months of the notification being released, reports Urban Acres . The detailed recruitment calendar will be released after receiving formal approval. Meanwhile, the final number of vacancies and their distribution across different categories will be determined based on the updated data being collected from healthcare facilities across all 38 districts. bihar_raw_news.title: Away From Bihar This Chhath Puja? Check These Ghats in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru
bihar_raw_news.content: ET Online From Yamuna-side ghats in Delhi and Juhu Beach in Mumbai to community-organised celebrations in Bengaluru, explore locations where devotees can observe Sandhya and Usha Arghya. (AI Image) For families who have moved away from Bihar for work, education or business, Chhath Puja is one festival that often brings the feeling of home back to their adopted city. Thekua, bamboo baskets, traditional folk songs and the evening and morning offerings to the Sun God become familiar sights even thousands of kilometres away from their hometowns. In 2026, Chhath Puja will be observed from November 13 to 16. While Nahay Khay falls on November 13 and Kharna on November 14, devotees will offer Sandhya Arghya on November 15 and Usha Arghya on November 16. If you are staying in Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru and cannot travel to Bihar this year, you do not necessarily have to celebrate alone. Community organisations, local committees and civic authorities facilitate celebrations at several water bodies and temporary ghats across these cities. Must Read: Chhath Puja 2026 Date: November 15 or 16? Check 4-Day Calendar, Nahay Khay, Kharna and Arghya Timings Here is a city-wise guide to locations worth checking before making your plans. Live Events Chhath Puja Ghats in Delhi: Where Can You Offer Arghya? Delhi has one of the largest networks of Chhath Puja celebration sites outside Bihar. The festival is observed across neighbourhoods with significant Purvanchali populations, with arrangements ranging from Yamuna-side ghats to temporary ponds and community-managed water bodies. The Delhi government has announced plans for more than 1,400 ghats in 2026. This means devotees may be able to find a celebration closer to their residential area instead of travelling across the city to a major riverfront location. Some locations to check include: 1. ITO Yamuna Ghat The ITO area is among the well-known locations for Chhath Puja celebrations in central Delhi. Devotees gather near the Yamuna to offer prayers during both Sandhya Arghya and Usha Arghya. Its central location makes it an option for people living in parts of central and east Delhi. However, expect significant crowds during the main ritual periods. Check the designated entry points and traffic restrictions before travelling. 2. Kalindi Kunj Ghat Kalindi Kunj is another prominent location associated with Chhath celebrations in Delhi. Families from south and southeast Delhi and nearby areas may find it more convenient than travelling to the central Yamuna ghats. Before leaving, confirm the exact ghat and permitted access route with the local organising committee. Traffic and entry arrangements can change during the festival. 3. Burari and Wazirabad-side ghats North Delhi has several locations where Chhath celebrations are organised around the Yamuna and designated community water bodies. Burari and the Wazirabad-side areas are worth checking for devotees living in north and northwest Delhi. Local committees may organise temporary arrangements, so the exact venue should be confirmed rather than assuming that every riverbank is open for rituals. 4. Dwarka Sector 11 DDA Ground Residents of Dwarka and nearby parts of southwest Delhi

national_raw_news.title: COP31 climate summit to begin in Antalya, Turkey today
national_raw_news.content: Leaders, scientists, civil society representatives, activists and others from nearly 200 countries, including India, are gathering for two weeks in Turkey’s Mediterranean resort city of Antalya for the 31st Conference of Parties to the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), beginning today, with aim to accelerate clean energy, scale up climate finance and strengthen resilience. The summit will continue till November 20. The Conference of the Parties (COP), the highest-level global climate summit held annually under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), is bringing together heads of state, Ministers, scientists, business leaders, and civil society representatives from around the world and serves as the primary platform for negotiating and advancing collective action to combat climate change. At COP31, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) will support countries by providing authoritative scientific observations and information on the state of the global climate system, including through the launch of its flagship State of Climate update 2026, a science-based annual assessment of climate indicators and impacts. This year’s climate summit is being held in the backdrop of the this month’s United Nations Environment Programme’s (UNEP) report that says with global warming set to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius, adaptation finance falls far short of needs, implementation is constrained by institutional barriers, and losses and damages are mounting.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 years. Addressing the jawans on the occasion of Diwali in Bastar, Chhattisgarh yesterday, Prime Minister compared India’s welfare architecture over the past 12 years to a Diwali Rangoli where small, distinct lines come together to form a grand picture. The Prime Minister detailed how Jan Dhan banking, PM Awas pucca homes, collateral-free Mudra loans, SVANidhi support for street vendors, Ayushman Bharat healthcare, free monthly rations, child education policies, Swachh Bharat, and Har Ghar Jal collectively ensured free medicine, free education, and a free kitchen while removing basic anxieties so families once trapped in generational poverty now inherit a stronger future. Prime Minister Modi said, the poor families whose entire lives used to be spent only in worry have now received the assurance of the government, and a new self-confidence has come into them. Pointing out that this victory over poverty is deeply linked to the fight against Naxalism, which previously trapped lakhs of innocent citizens in deprivation by blocking schools, hospitals, medical stores, polio vaccinations, mobile towers, and industries while bombing railway tracks, the Prime Minister detailed the special development drive in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas that built over 15,000 kilometres of roads, over 9,500 mobile towers, nearly 175 Eklavya schools, around 50 ITIs, 50 Skill Development Centres, and thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs, alongside rehabilitating surrendered Naxals and bringing water, electricity, and roads to remote tribal villages for the first time under PM JANMAN. Stating that the ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ campaign energized the fight against poverty and brought an end to Naxal violence alongside lifting 50 crore people out of extreme poverty, the Prime Minister cited the ongoing Bastar Olympics as a symbol of transformation in the region. Today in this very Bastar, the Bastar Olympics are taking place, and children are trying their hand at sports, not guns, remarked Shri Modi.

national_raw_news.title: BSF celebrates Diwali with personnel along India-Bangladesh border 4 hours ago 75
national_raw_news.content: The Border Security Force (BSF) celebrated Diwali with its Seema Praharis deployed at various border locations along the India-Bangladesh International Border yesterday with traditional festivities, distribution of sweets and a message of unity and brotherhood. A BSF spokesman said that Princee Rani, Inspector General (IG) of the BSF’s Tripura Frontier, joined the celebrations with the border personnel at different locations. The festivities featured the lighting of diyas, fireworks and distribution of sweets, spreading festive cheer and camaraderie among the troops guarding the country’s borders. During the celebrations, the IG appreciated the dedication, commitment and vigilance of the Seema Praharis in safeguarding the International Border and preventing trans-border crimes. She also acknowledged the sacrifices made by the personnel who remain away from their families during festivals and other important occasions to ensure the security of the nation. All BSF Commandants distributed sweets to their respective Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) counterparts across all sectors as a gesture of goodwill and festive camaraderie on the occasion of Diwali. Meanwhile, former Union Minister and BJP leader Pratima Bhowmik also celebrated the spirit of Diwali by exchanging festive greetings with BSF personnel and members of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) at the Akhaura Integrated Check Post in Agartala. In a social media post, Bhowmik said that BSF personnel remain deployed round the year along the International Border to ensure the security of the country. She said, while people across the country celebrate the festival of lights with their families, BSF personnel deployed along the borders remain away from their loved ones to protect the nation.
